detailed_description:
high angle,Twenty seconds of realistic nighttime domestic intimacy. Warm dim kitchen light and the fridge's softer cool spill preserve natural skin, not a dark horror grade. Strict human-eye POV, a single continuous shot with motivated head turns. The camera never leaves the viewer, shows his face, or switches to a two-person angle. No subtitles, captions, readable labels, title or watermark. The performance times below remain inside the same [Shot 1].

[Shot 1] During 0–4 seconds, the viewer quietly opens a refrigerator door toward the left of the frame with his left hand. He already holds one small fork in his right hand. The slightly guilty, slow movement and tiny pause before opening make his secret snack hunt readable. His fork hand enters the doorway but has not found the cake. From immediately to the right, Zhenzhen's sleepy voice, <Subject 1> (S1), says, <d>[Chinese] 第二层.</d> His right hand abruptly stops and retreats a few centimetres. Do not stage an exaggerated jump scare.

During 4–8 seconds, the viewer turns his head a short distance right, revealing <Subject 1> already standing beside the open door and the adjacent counter. She has not teleported from another room. Her long dark-brown hair is slightly relaxed, a cream blanket rests over her shoulders, and the same black thin-strap top remains visible. Both hands are free. She gives a small yawn, then an amused look at his guilty fork. She gently indicates the fridge's second shelf with her eyes and a small chin tilt, keeping the action natural.

During 8–12 seconds, she takes the small plate of cake from that second shelf using both hands and places it on the counter immediately to the viewer's right. The head turn follows the plate only as far as this neighbouring counter; keep her face and the cake legible in the same medium-close composition. She releases the plate completely, looks back at him and says, <Subject 1> (S1): <d>[Chinese] 给你留的, 没舍得吃.</d> Her hands relax near the counter. The open fridge remains on the left; its light does not vanish.

During 12–16 seconds, the viewer uses the fork he has held in his right hand since the opening to pick up one small bite from the stationary cake. He starts to bring it toward himself, then deliberately changes course and offers the first bite toward her. The camera follows with a small eye movement from the plate to her face, not a mechanical zoom. She notices the changed destination, glances once at the offered bite and then at his eyes. Her sleepy teasing expression softens with genuine surprise. Allow this recognition before she leans in.

During 16–20 seconds, she takes the small bite gently from the fork, and his right hand lowers the now-empty fork away from her mouth. She chews quietly without speaking. With one free hand she nudges the plate a few centimetres toward his side of the counter, making room for him beside her; she meets his eyes with a small private smile. The viewer leans a little closer to share the space. End with her response to his choice and the plate now between them, not a posed beauty shot. Hands, fork and plate keep their ownership; no extra utensils appear.

overall_soundscape:
Low refrigerator hum, a soft door seal opening, a faint fork-on-plate sound, quiet clothing rustle and gentle breathing. Zhenzhen's voice is close, soft and conversational, with sleepy warmth. Only she speaks. Leave a small silence after the offered first bite so her recognition is felt. No spoken lines while she is chewing, no voice-over narrator and no artificial audience laughter.
